peer_results.rationale: The retrieved candidates for AMD focus on industry consolidation (M&A) and outsourced logistics functions. These do not address the specific topic of periodic supply/capacity constraints incentivizing customer vertical integration or limiting supply, which is the core of QCOM's disclosure. Consolidation risk is a structural market change, while QCOM's risk is a cyclical supply constraint issue.

comparisons.peer_topic: Materials Supplier Concentration and Geopolitical Risks
comparisons.peer_summary: The company purchases ~two-thirds of manufacturing materials from five suppliers, some single-source, with no long-term contracts; supply constraints due to extended lead times, limited supplies, or U.S.-China trade tensions could disrupt supply and adversely impact operations.
comparisons.comparison: QCOM and AVGO both identify supply constraints as a driver of business risk within the semiconductor industry. QCOM notes that these constraints may incentivize customers to vertically integrate to secure supply chain control. AVGO discloses that suppliers may extend lead times, limit supplies, or place products on allocation due to similar constraints, which could disrupt AVGO's operations. Both disclosures recognize the scarcity of supply/capacity as a structural industry risk, with QCOM highlighting the strategic consequence (customer integration) and AVGO highlighting the operational consequence (supply disruption/pricing).

sentences.text: In addition, periodic supply/capacity constraints within the semiconductor industry may further incentivize our customers to vertically integrate in an effort to secure additional control over their supply chains.
Suppliers may extend lead times, limit supplies, place products on allocation or increase prices, any of which could disrupt supply or increase demand in the industry.
Any such supply constraints could result in loss of revenue opportunities and adversely impact our business, financial condition and results of operations.

comparisons.peer_topic: Global supply chain complexity and disruption risks
comparisons.peer_summary: Intel's complex global supply chain is susceptible to disruptions from supplier capacity constraints, quality issues, cyberattacks, and natural disasters, which can increase costs, delay shipments, and harm financial results.
comparisons.comparison: Both QCOM and INTC disclose that periodic supply or capacity constraints in the semiconductor industry negatively impact their operations. QCOM highlights that these constraints may incentivize customers to vertically integrate to secure control, whereas INTC details that such constraints (including extended lead times and capacity limitations) directly increase costs, disrupt production, and delay shipments for Intel. Both identify supply capacity as a critical vulnerability in the industry.

sentences.text: In addition, periodic supply/capacity constraints within the semiconductor industry may further incentivize our customers to vertically integrate in an effort to secure additional control over their supply chains.

▪suppliers extending lead times, experiencing capacity constraints, limiting or canceling supply, allocating supply to other customers including competitors, delaying or canceling deliveries, or increasing prices;

These and other supply chain issues can increase our costs, disrupt or reduce our production, delay our product shipments, prevent us from meeting customer demand, damage our customer relationships, or negatively affect our reputation.

comparisons.peer_topic: Supply chain dependency and material availability
comparisons.peer_summary: The supply chain depends on third-party providers and exacting material standards, with limited sources for certain components. Shortages of raw materials, chemicals, or silicon wafers, along with inflationary pressures and lack of long-term capacity commitments in contracts, may limit bit shipments, increase costs, or disrupt operations. Additionally, reliance on China for rare earth elements poses a risk if exports are restricted.
comparisons.comparison: QCOM and MU both address the risk of supply constraints limiting business outputs. QCOM notes that periodic supply/capacity constraints may drive customers to vertically integrate. MU specifies that constraints within its supply chain for materials and components could limit its bit shipments and adversely affect financial condition. Both disclosures link industry-wide supply capacity issues to tangible business risks, though QCOM focuses on the strategic reaction of customers (vertical integration) while MU focuses on the direct impact on its own shipment volumes and costs.

sentences.text: In addition, periodic supply/capacity constraints within the semiconductor industry may further incentivize our customers to vertically integrate in an effort to secure additional control over their supply chains.

Constraints within our supply chain for certain materials and integrated circuit components could limit our bit shipments, which could have a material adverse effect on our business, results of operations, or financial condition.

To the extent we do not have firm commitments from our third-party suppliers over a specific time period or for any specific capacity, quantity, and/or pricing, our suppliers may allocate capacity to their other customers and capacity and/or materials may not be available when needed or at reasonable prices.

comparisons.peer_summary: The company builds finished products and maintains inventory in advance of anticipated demand, entering into long-term supply and capacity commitments which may not be sufficient if revenue declines. Demand for data center products surged in fiscal 2024, and next-generation products are expected to be supply-constrained; the company has increased supply purchases and added vendors, which increases complexity and execution risk.
comparisons.comparison: Both QCOM and NVDA discuss the risks associated with securing supply and capacity in the face of industry constraints. QCOM states that periodic supply/capacity constraints incentivize customers to vertically integrate to secure control. NVDA discloses that it has entered into long-term supply and capacity commitments to address potential insufficiencies, and that during periods of shortage, lead times may be extended. Both companies acknowledge that supply capacity is a finite resource that requires proactive management or strategic shifts (like customer vertical integration at QCOM or long-term commitments/premiums at NVDA) to mitigate risk.

sentences.text: In addition, periodic supply/capacity constraints within the semiconductor industry may further incentivize our customers to vertically integrate in an effort to secure additional control over their supply chains.

While we have in the past entered and may in the future enter into long-term supply and capacity commitments, we may not be able to secure sufficient commitments for capacity to address our business needs, or our long-term demand expectations may change.
In periods of shortages impacting the semiconductor industry and/or limited supply or capacity in our supply chain, the lead times on our orders may be extended.
